key_insight: Single-crystal Ti-15Mo shows inverted orientation-dependent elasticity and yield onset, with <111>-near surfaces unexpectedly the softest and not explainable by simple Schmid-factor/CRSS predictions.
engineering_relevance: Texture and grain orientation in Ti-15Mo can materially change local compliance and incipient plasticity, so processing routes must account for single-grain anisotropy when targeting reliable wrought-component performance.
method: EBSD-guided nanoindentation on surfaces near <111>, <124>, <011>, <023>, and <013> crystallographic normals
Measured indentation modulus, hardness, strain-rate sensitivity, and yield onset across orientations
Performed strain-rate-jump analysis to estimate activation volume and infer deformation mechanism groups
evidence_signal: The abstract reports only ~10% modulus anisotropy, 41% spread in yield onset, 6.6% hardness spread, and activation volumes of 18–31 b^3 that separate the orientations into two response groups.
watch_item: The proposed retained athermal ω-phase explanation is inferential from indentation data, so direct phase/microstructure confirmation would be needed before using it as a design rule.
paper_title: Orientation-Resolved Nanoindentation of Single Crystal Ti-15Mo: Inverted Elastic Anisotropy and Yield-Onset Behavior Beyond Simple CRSS Predictions
